implementation_notes: Resolve us_code by linear scan of country_code dict (113-ish entries).
Resolve cn_ids by scanning company_name rows where country_code==us_code and name=='YouTube' (exact len=7 memcmp).
Resolve it1_id by linear scan of info_type.info dict (113 rows) for 'release dates'.
For each cn_id in cn_ids, iterate CSR slice [mc_co_off[cn_id], mc_co_off[cn_id+1]) -> mc row r.
Apply mc.note LIKE checks via two memmem calls (substrings '(200' + ')' approximated as memmem '(200' AND memmem '(worldwide)').
Compute mv = mc.movie_id[r]; title row index = mv-1; check production_year in [2005,2010] (skip INT32_MIN).
Existence via offsets_only: aka_off[mv]<aka_off[mv+1] and mk_off[mv]<mk_off[mv+1].
Walk movie_info: for k in [mi_off[mv], mi_off[mv+1]) check info_type_id[k]==it1_id, then memmem('internet') on note, then prefix 'USA:' and memmem(' 200') on info; update mins.
MIN compares: lexicographic memcmp on (ptr,len); track best as (off,len).
Final output formats best title and best mi.info from their .dat buffers.
